Placement on site:y2l-yangyang: COSINE-100 sat in the A5 tunnel of Y2L.
The COSINE-100 full-data-set paper puts Y2L at about 1,800 m water equivalent; the KIMS papers say 2000-2400 m.w.e. (see site:y2l-yangyang).
A 2026 preprint (arXiv:2610.19668) lowers the analysis threshold of the full six-year data set to 0.49 keV; it is not recorded as a result because it reports an expected sensitivity.

physics_goals.quote: The COSINE-100 experiment, consisting of 106 kg of NaI(Tl) target material, is designed to carry out a model-independent test of DAMA/LIBRA's claim of WIMP discovery by searching for the same annual modulation signal using the same NaI(Tl) target.
physics_goals.value: Model-independent test of DAMA/LIBRA's annual-modulation claim with the same NaI(Tl) target

summary.plain: COSINE-100 was a 106 kg array of eight sodium-iodide crystals at the Yangyang underground laboratory, built to test the long-disputed claim by the DAMA experiment of a yearly rise and fall in dark-matter-like signals, using the same kind of crystal. It ran from 2016 to 2023 and has not confirmed the DAMA signal.
summary.technical: Eight NaI(Tl) crystals (106 kg, two 3-inch PMTs each) immersed in 2,200 L of LAB liquid scintillator (active veto) inside a copper box, a 20 cm lead castle and plastic-scintillator muon panels, in the Y2L A5 tunnel (700 m overburden). Physics data 21 Oct 2016 - 14 Mar 2023 (6.4 yr). Annual-modulation analyses (1.7 yr, 3 yr, 6.4 yr full data set), WIMP limits with a 1 keV and then 0.7 keV threshold, and a combined analysis with ANAIS-112.
